clinicalPearls: Group of inherited disorders defined by profound impairment of T-cell development, with variable B-cell and natural killer cell involvement, causing severe combined immune failure
Affected infants typically present in the first months of life with recurrent, severe, or opportunistic infections, chronic diarrhoea, and failure to thrive
Persistent or unusual infections such as Pneumocystis pneumonia, chronic candidiasis, and disseminated viral disease are characteristic
Absence of a thymic shadow and marked lymphopenia are important early clues
Genetic causes are heterogeneous and include X-linked common gamma-chain defects, adenosine deaminase deficiency, and several autosomal recessive gene defects
Newborn screening using T-cell receptor excision circles enables presymptomatic detection and early treatment
Definitive treatment is immune reconstitution, principally haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, with gene therapy and enzyme replacement for specific subtypes
Early diagnosis before infections develop markedly improves transplant outcomes
reference.pathophysiology: Severe combined immunodeficiency comprises a genetically diverse group of disorders that share a failure of adaptive immunity due to absent or non-functional T lymphocytes, with associated defects in B-cell and sometimes natural killer cell function. Underlying defects disrupt lymphocyte development or function through varied mechanisms, such as impaired cytokine receptor signalling in common gamma-chain deficiency, toxic metabolite accumulation in adenosine deaminase deficiency, or failure of antigen-receptor gene rearrangement. Without functional T cells, the coordinated immune response to pathogens collapses, leaving infants unable to clear common and opportunistic organisms. Most forms are inherited in an autosomal recessive manner, with the common gamma-chain form being X-linked.
additionalDifferentials: Other combined immunodeficiencies of lesser severity
DiGeorge syndrome with severe thymic hypoplasia
additionalInvestigations: Newborn screening for low T-cell receptor excision circles where available
Full blood count with lymphocyte subset quantification
Immunoglobulin levels and functional lymphocyte proliferation studies
Molecular genetic testing to define the specific subtype
Adenosine deaminase enzyme assay and chest imaging for thymic assessment
redFlags: This is a paediatric emergency: suspected SCID requires immediate specialist referral and protective isolation
Live vaccines, including BCG and rotavirus, are contraindicated and can cause fatal disseminated infection
Blood products must be irradiated, cytomegalovirus-safe, and leucodepleted to prevent transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease
Any infection can rapidly become life-threatening and needs urgent aggressive management
reference.prognosis: Without immune reconstitution the condition is usually fatal within the first year or two of life, but early haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, particularly before infections occur, offers a high chance of long-term survival and immune recovery.
pitfalls: Administering live vaccines before immunodeficiency is excluded
Delaying referral by attributing recurrent infections to ordinary childhood illness
Overlooking lymphopenia on a routine full blood count
management: Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is the definitive curative therapy, ideally performed early before infections develop
Gene therapy for selected genotypes and enzyme replacement with pegademase for adenosine deaminase deficiency as a bridge
Protective isolation and strict infection-prevention measures pending immune reconstitution
Antimicrobial prophylaxis against Pneumocystis with co-trimoxazole, plus antifungal and antiviral cover
Immunoglobulin replacement therapy to cover the antibody deficiency
Use only irradiated, cytomegalovirus-safe, leucodepleted blood products and withhold live vaccines
Genetic counselling, carrier testing, and family screening, with newborn screening of siblings
Manage through immunology and transplant multidisciplinary teams
